title: Comment On Pro-Soviet Book Entitled Our Time Alleged To Have Been Published In Shanghai

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. 2, Special Branch.
REPORT
File No. S.B. REGISTRY.
Date December 15, 1934.
Subject (in full) Comment on pro-Soviet book entitled "Our Time"
alleged to have been published in Shanghai.
Made by I.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by [Signature]

With reference to the endorsement of V.C. (Special
Branch) on the attached report dated December 11, 1934, on the
subject of seizure by the Manzhukuo authorities in Harbin of
N.V. Ustrialoff's pro-Soviet book in Russian entitled "Our Time",
which is alleged to have been published by the "Centurion Printing
Co.", 126 Nanzing Road, enquiries show that this book has not
been on sale in Shanghai and is not available at local Russian
libraries. A copy of the book was borrowed for perusal by
the undersigned from a person, to whom it had been presented
by the author.

It appears that the book in question was published
in Shanghai in 1934, but it contains no mention of the place,
where it was printed. It consists of 202 pages and is divided
into two parts entitled "From the New Economic Policy towards
the Soviet Socialism" and "The Ways of Synthesis" respectively.
Each part contains a series of articles, some of which were
previously published in Harbin and Tientsin newspapers, while
the other appear in print for the first time.

Articles contained in the first part are devoted
to fundamental political problems of the Soviet Union and are
intended to reflect the significance and dramatic character
of the past few years. Assertion that the Soviet Socialism
has definitely won its battle fought under most difficult
and complicated conditions-is the key-note of these articles,
of which the one entitled "After the XVII-th Congress", presents
the main interest.

The second part of the book contains articles, which
are described by the author as "essays on the philosophy of the
present epoch". Professor Ustrialoff is not and never was a

主题（全称） 对据称在上海出版的亲苏书籍《我们的时代》的评论
由 I.S.I. Prokofiev 撰写。转呈人 [签名]

关于附后之1934年12月11日报告上 V.C.（特科）的批注，该报告涉及满洲国当局在哈尔滨查扣 N.V. Ustrialoff 所著俄文亲苏书籍《我们的时代》一事，据称该书由南京路126号“百夫长印刷公司”（Centurion Printing Co.）出版。经查询，此书并未在上海发售，本地俄文图书馆亦无馆藏。下述签署人从一位受作者赠书的人士处借得一本以供阅览。

据悉，该书于1934年在上海出版，但书中未提及印刷地点。全书共202页，分为两部分，标题分别为“从新经济政策走向苏维埃社会主义”和“综合之路”。每部分包含一系列文章，其中一些此前曾在哈尔滨和天津的报纸上发表过，另一些则是首次刊印。

第一部分的文章致力于探讨苏联的根本政治问题，旨在反映过去几年的重要意义及其戏剧性特征。这些文章的基调是断言苏维埃社会主义在最艰难和复杂的条件下进行的斗争已取得决定性胜利，其中以题为“第十七次代表大会之后”的文章最引人关注。

本书第二部分包含被作者描述为“当今时代哲学随笔”的文章。Ustrialoff 教授并非，也从未是一名

communist. Together with the bulk of the Russian intelligentsia
he refused to co-operate with the Bolsheviks during the first
period of their rule in Russia and at the time of the civil war
he was with the "Whites". His opponents, however, maintain
that his position during that period was neutral and that he
merely was awaiting the outcome of the struggle with a view to
eventually taking the side of the "top-dog", irrespective of its
political colour. Indeed, immediately following the final
defeat of the "Whites" in 1920 he became a prominent advocate
of loyalty towards the Soviet government inspite of his inner
scepticism regarding the success of the bolshevist programme.
He was not altogether free of this scepticism in 1930, when he
wrote: "Should the revolutionary programme-maximum and the
planned reorganization of the country prove a success, how can
we help exclaiming with joy "Thou hast conquered, o Galillean!"
At present, in the light of events of the past four years, he
has cast off his last doubts and welcomes the Soviet victory
and the ambition of bolsheviks to organize a "Classless Society".
        Whether he is sincere in his praises is another
question. There are indications that the bolshevist leaders
including Stalin are rather doubtful about this point, although
the general attitude of the Soviet authorities towards Ustrialoff
has been that of benevolence and he was given a post in the
Education Department of the Chinese Eastern Railway in Harbin.
It is also significant that, with the exception of one visit to
the USSR in 1926, he has been residing in Harbin ever since 1920.
        His critics from the opposite camp describe him as
being a cynic devoid of any principles. To these accusations
Ustrialoff replies: "Yes, in your eyes I must look cynical. I

共产主义者。他与大多数俄国知识分子一起，在布尔什维克统治俄国的初期拒绝与其合作，在内战期间他站在“白军”一边。然而，他的反对者坚持认为，他在那一时期的立场是中立的，他 merely 只是在等待斗争的结果，以便最终倒向“胜者”，不论其政治色彩如何。事实上，在1920年“白军”最终溃败后，尽管他对布尔什维克纲领的成功持内心怀疑态度，但他成为了效忠苏维埃政府的著名倡导者。他在1930年写作时并未完全摆脱这种怀疑，当时他写道：“如果革命的最高纲领和国家的计划重组证明是成功的，我们怎能不欣喜地高呼‘加利利人，你征服了！’”目前，鉴于过去四年的事件，他已摒弃最后的疑虑，欢迎苏维埃的胜利以及布尔什维克组织“无阶级社会”的抱负。
        他的赞扬是否真诚则是另一个问题。有迹象表明，包括斯大林在内的布尔什维克领导人对这一点相当怀疑，尽管苏维埃当局对 Ustrialoff 的总体态度一直是善意的，并且他在哈尔滨的中东铁路教育部获得了一个职位。同样值得注意的是，除了1926年访问苏联一次外，自1920年以来他一直居住在哈尔滨。

appreciate our poets and philosophers and at the same time I
refuse to see in Lenin an "escaped convict". I do not think
that the Russian revolution means death, or shame or is a
misunderstanding. I studied moral philosophy at the university
of Moscow - and I do not curse the godless Bolshevism! It is
beyond your ability to understand me and your insults are for
me only another proof of the deep, dreadful and beautiful
complexity of life."

Ustrialoff's reputation as a clever publicist is
well established. The book under review is undoubtedly of
a strongly pro-Soviet character, and is likely to create
impression desired by the author upon the minds of readers,
especially among Russian emigrants' youth. It must be pointed out,
however, that the author treats his subject in an abstract,
academic manner.

In the opinion of the undersigned the book in question
contains nothing which would warrant an action on the part of
the Municipal Police against the person or persons responsible
for its publishing.

                                        G. Prokofiev
                                        D. S. I.

欣赏我们的诗人和哲学家，同时我拒绝将列宁视为‘逃犯’。我不认为俄国革命意味着死亡、耻辱或是一种误解。我在莫斯科大学学习道德哲学——我并不诅咒无神论的布尔什维主义！你们无法理解我，你们的侮辱对我而言只是生活深刻、可怕而又美丽的复杂性的又一证明。”

Ustrialoff 作为一位精明宣传家的声誉已确立。这本受评书籍无疑具有强烈的亲苏性质，可能会在读者心中，尤其是俄国流亡青年中，产生作者所期望的印象。然而，必须指出的是，作者以抽象、学术的方式处理其主题。

在下述签署人看来，涉案书籍不包含任何足以证明工部局警务处对其出版负责人采取行动的理由。

                                        G. Prokofiev
                                        D. S. I.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. S. 2, Special Branch Statist.
REPORT
Date December 10, 1934.

Subject (in full) Pro-Soviet book entitled "Our Time" seized by the Manchoukuo
Authorities at Harbin.
Made by D. S. Umemoto. Forwarded by J B Loo A.

Information has been received by the local Japanese Consular
Police from the Harbin Consular Police to the effect that several
copies of a Russian book of pro-Soviet nature entitled "Our Time"
have been seized at Harbin. Upon being question by the Manchoukuo
Authorities, H.B. Ustrialoff, the author of this book, who is a
professor at the Politic-Technical Institution in Harbin, made
the following statement:- "In June this year, I requested N. S.
Zephiroff, a resident in Shanghai, to print some 300 copies of
the book. I understand that they were printed at the Centurion
Printing Company in Shanghai by order of Zephiroff. A friend of
mine who came from Shanghai brought to me 40 copies several of
which I have already delivered to Moscow, the Soviet Embassy at
Tokyo and other places. I do not remember the name of the person
who brought the book to me. I do not know what Zephiroff is
doing in Shanghai."
N. S. Zephiroff is connected with "The New World", a daily
Russian-English newspaper of pro-Soviet tendencies published in
Shanghai. Centurion Printing Company has its office at No. 126
Nanking Road.

M Umemoto.
D. S.

D. C., Special Branch.
S2,
Ray.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
档案号 S. 2，特科统计。
报告
日期 1934年12月10日。

主题（全称） 满洲国当局在哈尔滨查扣的亲苏书籍《我们的时代》。
由 D. S. Umemoto 撰写。转呈人 J B Loo A.

本地日本领事警察收到哈尔滨领事警察的情报，称在哈尔滨查扣了数本名为《我们的时代》的俄文亲苏书籍。经满洲国当局讯问，该书作者、哈尔滨政治技术学院教授 H.B. Ustrialoff 作出如下陈述：“今年六月，我请求居住在上海的 N. S. Zephiroff 印刷约300册该书。据我所知，这些书是 Zephiroff 下令在上海的百夫长印刷公司印刷的。我的一位从上海来的朋友给我带来了40册，其中几册我已寄往莫斯科、驻东京的苏联大使馆及其他地方。我不记得把书带给我的人的名字。我不知道 Zephiroff 在上海做什么。”
N. S. Zephiroff 与《新世界》有关联，这是一份在上海出版的具有亲苏倾向的俄英双语日报。百夫长印刷公司的办公地址位于南京路126号。

M Umemoto.
D. S.

Ray.
